subject: Term flexibility and activation timeline for Dedicated pool — phase-in proposal
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbus-systems.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kate Li <kate.li@nimbus-systems.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool — initial sizing, term flexibility, and start window

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Nimbus is evaluating several vendors for a dedicated inference pool to power our real-time personalization API. A couple of follow-ups from product and procurement:

- We expect ~1200 concurrent small-context requests at peak, ~45M tokens/day. We think this maps to a ~12-GPU pool with room for burst, but we wanted Redwood's sizing guidance.
- Procurement prefers a 12-month term but can consider 24/36 with deeper discounts. Is there room for a blended ramp with a shorter initial commit?
- Important: need a clear activation/start date with a soft phase-in (first 30 days staging at reduced capacity, then full capacity by month 2).
- Also attach a short requirements spreadsheet (attached) and our standard redlines will come from legal.

Can you provide a few term + ramp options (pricing, discount, SLA credits) and the earliest possible activation date if we sign next week?

Best,
Alex
Director of Product, Nimbus Systems

Attachments: Nimbus_Dedicated_Requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet, 23KB)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@nimbus-systems.com>
Cc: Kate Li <kate.li@nimbus-systems.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — initial sizing, term flexibility, and start window

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear requirements and the sheet. Looping in Neha (onboarding/ops) and Priyom (SE) to align on sizing and an activation cadence. High-level options below — I'll follow up with a formal commercial sheet and a SOW draft.

Proposal (starter options):

1) 12-month (lowest commitment)
- Committed pool: 8 gpus reserved, ability to burst to 12 (usage billed on burst).
- Discount: 10% off list for reserved units.
- Ramp: staging window 30 days (50% reserved capacity), full capacity by day 45.
- SLA: 99.5% uptime target; SLA credit up to 5% monthly if missed.

2) 24-month (recommended for predictable unit cost)
- Committed pool: 10 gpus reserved, burst to 14.
- Discount: 18% off list.
- Ramp: 30-day staging, linear increase to full capacity by day 60 (phased buckets).
- SLA: 99.7% uptime; SLA credit up to 7%.

3) 36-month (max discount, capacity guarantees)
- Committed pool: 12 gpus reserved, burst to 18.
- Discount: 25% off list + 2 months free if signed in current fiscal quarter.
- Ramp: pilot week (reduced 30% capacity), month 1 at 60%, full by month 2.
- SLA: 99.8% uptime; SLA credit tier up to 10% and capacity buyback clause for first 6 months.

Notes/assumptions:
- Throughput guarantees are model-dependent; we'll size by tail-latency targets (95th percentile) and typical seq length. Priyom: can you confirm the 1200 concurrent and tokens/day mapping to GPU SKU we recommend?
- Activation: earliest start is ~10 business days after signed SOW + PO (for provisioning and network setup) assuming no legal blocking.
- We can accommodate a hybrid ramp (start smaller on a 12-month with option to convert to 24/36 with a retroactive credit).

Next steps: Priyom and Neha to propose an exact GPU SKU mapping and a detailed ramp calendar. I'll draft a commercial summary and include a DocuSign-ready MSA + SOW.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0136
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — initial sizing, term flexibility, and start window

Rishi / Neha — reviewed the Nimbus sheet. Quick technical readout and recommendation: 

- Baseline perf: for the family of models they described (small-context personalization ~1k tokens/session), an A10G-equivalent gives ~95 requests/s per GPU at p95 < 120ms when batched with our runtime optimizations.
- For 1200 concurrent: we recommend starting with 10 gpus to keep p95 latency headroom, then scale to 14 within 6 weeks if traffic behaves as forecast.
- Burst: implement dynamic burst pool (shared across tenant) with soft budget caps; billing on burst to avoid over-reserving.
- Ramp calendar proposal (detailed):
  * Day 0: Provision 6 GPUs (network + infra validation).
  * Day 7–30: Stage to 8 GPUs (validation load, 50–70% traffic routing).
  * Day 31–60: Increase to 10–12 GPUs depending on telemetry.
  * Month 3: target 12–14 GPUs steady state.

Operational asks for Nimbus:
- Provide representative traffic traces or replay if possible.
- Whitelist CIDR ranges for early testing.

I'll produce an SKU map and expected monthly token cost delta by tomorrow EOD.

— Priyom
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — initial sizing, term flexibility, and start window

Internal ops notes / commercial levers we can use when negotiating: 

- Creditable staging: allow first 30 days at 50% committed billing for onboarding (good for procurement to accept a 12-mo deal).
- Convertibility: built-in conversion option to move from 12 -> 24 within first 90 days with retroactive rate adjustment (we can apply credit equal to difference in discount).
- SLA tightening: offer a 14-day remedy period before SLA credits apply for early ramp items.
- Capacity buyback: for 36mo deals, offer a partial buyback for the first 6 months (reduces financial risk for Nimbus).
- Legal: redlines in their MSA likely around data residency and audit rights — recommend we offer a limited SOC2 attestation addendum rather than full audit access at the outset.

I'll prepare a one-page commercial summary and run the extended SLA/credit language by legal.

— Neha
Head of Customer Onboarding, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool — initial sizing, term flexibility, and start window

Alex / Kate — following up with a consolidated offer based on your ask and our internal alignment. Attached: Draft_MSA_Nimbus_v1.docx and a short commercial summary (high-level below).

Consolidated proposal (summary):
- Pilot path (procurement-friendly): 12-month term, 8 reserved GPUs, burst to 12. First 30 days billed at 50% reserved rate for onboarding. Convertibility to 24-month within 90 days with credit for difference in rate. Estimated monthly cost (reserved portion): $XXX,XXX (detailed commercial sheet attached).
- Predictable path (recommended): 24-month term, 10 reserved GPUs, burst to 14. 18% discount off list, SLA 99.7% with 7% credit cap, linear ramp to full capacity by day 60.
- Strategic path (capacity guarantee): 36-month term, 12 reserved GPUs, burst to 18. 25% discount + 2 free months this quarter, capacity buyback for first 6 months, SLA 99.8% with 10% credit cap.

Activation timeline: earliest start ~10 business days post-signature; pilot provisioning can begin in ~5 business days with an approved PO and network access for staging.

Attachments: Draft_MSA_Nimbus_v1.docx (MS Word, 65KB).

Next steps: If you prefer, we can prepare a PO-ready commercial summary for procurement and a DocuSign link for the MSA/SOW. Happy to set a call with Neha and Priyom to walk the technical and onboarding plan.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
